$description: Shokunin Crafthouse · Semantic tokens · purpose-mapped aliases · Light + Dark modes. Every $value is a DTCG reference to a primitive — no hex or px lives in this file. The default $value resolves to the LIGHT mode value; the DARK mode value lives in $extensions.modes.dark. Build tools that don't understand the modes extension still get a valid light-mode token tree.

$metadata.modeStrategy: Each token's $value is the light-mode resolution. $extensions.modes.{light,dark} holds the full per-mode map so any DTCG processor can pick the right alias per theme. Mode-invariant tokens (spacing) repeat the same alias in both modes — explicit, no implicit fallback.
$metadata.aliasRule: Semantic tokens MUST alias primitives via the {group.subgroup.name} DTCG reference syntax. Hardcoded hex / px values in this file are a bug and will fail Sprint 1 success criterion 1b.

page.$description: Page ground. Foundation surface in both modes. Light = oatmeal warmGray.100, dark = warm near-black.

sunk.$description: Set-in component surface · cards, frames, tiles. In light, sits BELOW page (deeper). In dark, sits ABOVE page (lighter). Role-named for light-mode semantics; perceptual direction inverts in dark.

deepSunk.$description: Deeper-step surface · nested states, form inputs, card hover. One step beyond surface.sunk in either mode.

primary.$description: Primary text · body, headlines, strong rules. AAA on every surface in both modes.

secondary.$description: Secondary text · eyebrows, metadata, descriptions. AA on surface.page (5.0:1) and surface.sunk (4.6:1). USAGE RESTRICTION: must not render on surface.deepSunk in light mode — the pair drops to 4.04:1 (below AA). On deepest surface, use text.primary instead. Dark mode passes AA on all three surfaces.

usageRestrictions.reason: Contrast ratio 4.04:1 falls below WCAG AA 4.5:1 threshold on this pair only.

disabled.$description: Disabled text · placeholders, ghosted controls. Documented exception: fails AA by spec.

onAccent.$description: Text on shu/brand fills. Pure white reads strong against vermilion in both modes.

default.$description: Default 1px solid hairline. Structural dividers, title block, section rules.

subtle.$description: Dashed inner divisions. Secondary structural rules inside cards and sections.

strong.$description: Strong frame border. Title block, masthead, asserted structural frames.

focus.$description: Focus ring color. Shu in light mode, shu.400 (lifted) in dark for visibility.

default.$description: Resting state for interactive elements · button text + border. Ink in light, near-white in dark.

hover.$description: Hover state · primary button text/icon/border turn shu. Documented AA exception at 11px (3.8:1 on bg); brand-signal use justifies. Dark mode uses shu.400 for visibility.

active.$description: Pressed/active state · one step deeper than hover. Visual color slot exists; primary press is also a scale transform (motion.scale.pressButton 0.985).

success.$description: Success state · warm olive on light, lifted olive on dark. AA on respective grounds.

warning.$description: Warning state · deep ochre on light, lifted ochre on dark. AA on respective grounds.

error.$description: Error state · vermilion in both modes (lifted to shu.400 in dark). Same as brand accent — error and brand share the chromatic signal.

info.$description: Info state · warm slate on light, lifted slate on dark. AA on respective grounds.

accent.$description: Brand accent · vermilion shu kept consistent across modes for brand-mark continuity. Used for the mark, stamps, and signature surfaces — not body text.

accentDeep.$description: Brand accent deep · pressed accent state and AA-passing accent text on light surfaces (5.3:1 on warmGray.100).

text-on-inverse.$description: Sprint 4 addition · text on inverted surface. Tooltip body text and similar inverse-ground content. Near-white on light mode (atop dark Tooltip), ink on dark mode (atop light Tooltip).

surface-inverse.$description: Sprint 4 addition · inverted surface. Tooltip ground. Ink in light mode, near-white in dark mode — always the visual opposite of surface.page.
